guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Some manipulative people are too smart to present themselves as perfect. They present themselves as gifted but wounded, flawed but honest, dangerous but self-aware, so that every warning about them gets absorbed into a story of nuance, compassion, and spiritual maturity. The Protector must notice when compassion for someone starts excusing what your evidence already knows. An admission like “I have honesty issues and I’m working on them” may itself be honest; it is also evidence that an honesty problem currently exists. Self-awareness is not the same as correction.
brief:
- the main point: some manipulative people are too smart to look perfect; they present themselves as flawed but honest, wounded, self-aware, so every warning about them gets absorbed into a story about how deep and honest they are; the Protector notices when compassion for someone starts excusing what your evidence already knows; an admitted flaw may be honest and is also evidence the flaw exists now; self-awareness isn't correction.
- what the dedup leaves to add (experiments/t56-guide/DEDUP-REPORT.md, group 11): all of it (G11.1, G11.2 and G11.4 NEW; G11.3 and G11.5 PARTLY: compassion as what does the excusing, and someone else's self-awareness taken as the fix).
- already in the article, so not said again: "If they promise to change, that's probably as useful as their prior promises were." (Also Look Outward); a spiritual story explaining away a real boundary crossing ("karmic partner mirroring").
- stance (STANCE-LEDGER.md): keep "Some" manipulative people; keep that the admission "may itself be honest"; the article says a flaw doesn't prove they're manipulating you (Also Look Outward).
